messages:
erin: Heads-up — running long-context stress (200k tokens) and seeing steady KV cache growth on MI250 farm. After ~45m the process memory climbs and page-table shows lots of small 'holes' being created during spills. attaching short trace.

miguel: rough numbers? allocations vs evictions?

erin: quick snapshot: pagewalks/sec jumped ~3x right before growth, evict completions lags. tail token latency spikes ~60ms. repro cmd:

```
./run_longctx.sh --model paged-attn-test --steps 200000 --batch 8 --device mi250x --kv-pager=enabled --stats=trace.json
```

eric: can you paste the trace snippet? even a few lines helps.

erin: pasted below (trimmed):
```
[PAGER] spill_page id=0x7f9a ... size=16k -> remap -> success
[PT] mark_hole idx=12345 owner=0x3fa epoch=42
[WALK] pagewalk miss -> schedule async_eviction owner=0x3fa
[PT] remap idx=12345 -> new_page=0x8b1
[PT] hole_count++ -> 7
```

anita: hmm. "mark_hole" followed by remap then hole_count++ suggests we might be double-counting when remap races with async eviction completion. Did you see any stale owner refs?

erin: yes a couple of lines show owner ptrs differing between mark and eviction completion.

sam: fyi we recently changed kernel selection for spill_writer on MI series to use tiled kernels (stride-friendly). Could be causing different ordering of writes to shadow map vs main PT on MI250. H100 had a different path earlier which didn't surface.

miguel: that matches. On MI250 the writeback path batches and completes out-of-order relative to PT updates; the PT shadow writes assume in-order completion. If a remap races and reclaims the slot early we get a transient hole flagged but later reinsert — if counters aren't decremented correctly we leak hole_count.

maya: can you reproduce on H100? is this MI-only?

erin: quick test: h100 run same script, growth stays flat, evict completions remain steady. So probably MI-specific.

ci-bot: test longctx/kv_pager_mi250x failed on step 523 (memory growth). Uploading logs: s3://ci/longctx/1777777777/trace.log

devops-bot: suggestion — run with NVLINK off or single-GPU to see if cross-GPU ordering is involved. NVLINK ordering model differs on MI.

eric: profiling numbers from the MI run (sampled):
- pagewalks/sec: 8900 -> 27000 pre-growth
- avg evict completion latency: 2.1ms -> 12.4ms
- hole_count steady growth: +1 every ~2k tokens

anita: propose adding a per-pt-entry epoch field and compare on completion to avoid double-decrement. But watch for memory overhead. Alternative: convert hole_count to atomic compare-and-saturating decrement at reclaim.

miguel: I'd rather keep metadata minimal. Maybe we can change eviction completion to verify current owner matches expected before updating hole counters. That requires reading PT entry under lock or CAS.

erin: any quick mitigation we can patch into runtime before next deck validation?

sam: short-term: revert tiled spill_writer kernel selection on MI250 to previous linear kernel. That should restore write ordering semantics. It's a config flip.

miguel: agree, quick revert + assert added in PT reclaim path to detect owner mismatch will give us signal.

anita: I'll draft a small test that races remap+evict in a tight loop to reproduce deterministically. If we can get a unit test, we can prevent regressions.

erin: created bug: RDW-7123, tags: p1, kvcache, mi250. Attached minimal repro and trace link. Assigning to @miguel and @anita.

miguel: taking it. i'll try the kernel revert and run the stress matrix across h100/mi250/rtx.

erin: thanks — will monitor CI and push the temporary kernel selection rollback if tests agree. please add any logs to the bug. :thumbsup:

anita: also flagging this for runtime perf meeting tomorrow — kernel selection heuristics may need a spec for ordering guarantees.

erin: noted. next update in thread after first green run or failing repro.
